newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S TAROM AIRLINE HIKES DOMESTIC AIR FARES.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S TAROM AIRLINE HIKES DOMESTIC AIR FARES.

text.p: Romania's state-owned Tarom SA airline said on Tuesday it increased by some 85 percent its domestic passenger air fares and tripled cargo tariffs, following recent fuel price hikes.
"The measure was dictated by a 70 percent rise in kerosene prices, as well as increases in costs for operating on domestic airports," Tarom marketing director Gheorghe Lazaroiu said.
He said prices for international flights did not change.

The increase still placed Tarom's domestic route prices below those of its local competitor, private DacAir airliner, Lazaroiu said. Cargo fares tripled for internal routes of more than 400 km (256 miles) to reach 3,500 lei (80 cents) per kilo.

Tarom operates Russian-made AN-24s on 14 domestic routes and has recently acquired a French-made ATR aircraft for its most popular flight from Bucharest to Timisoara, on the western border with Yugoslavia and Hungary.
A one-way ticket to Timisoara will cost 110,000 lei ($25) starting January 16, up from 63,000 lei ($14.4 previously.
Transport minister Traian Basescu said rail passenger and cargo fares will also go up after increases in electricity and heating prices, expected later this month.
